previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for progressive dyspnea and increased sputum production in the setting of tracheostomy and recurrent tracheobronchial stenosis. He was found to have tracheobronchitis due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by sputum and bronchial cultures. He was treated with IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, and received two bronchoscopies with balloon dilation of the trachea and left main bronchus. His prednisone dose was increased to 20 mg daily to reduce airway inflammation and then tapered. A new humidifier was arranged due to risk of equipment contamination. He improved clinically, maintained oxygenation on room air, and was discharged home with follow-up planned in pulmonary and infectious disease clinics.
